description: CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, invoked as the @Service it became. LS-DATE='2022-06-31' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='YYYY-MM-DD' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (L84-L85); LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (L86) is the output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. No EXEC PGM= anywhere names this program - it is CALLed four times from two online programs, CORPT00C L392 and L412 and COTRN02C L393 and L413 - so it is a SERVICE and there is no PARM to declare. It opens no file either: the 157 lines carry no ENVIRONMENT DIVISION, no SELECT and no FD, only WORKING-STORAGE (L22) and LINKAGE (L83), so it seeds no dataset, writes no record and leaves no final state. Its entire observable behaviour is the 80 bytes L97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity L98 moves into RETURN-CODE, here 3. Arm 3 of the ten-arm EVALUATE TRUE at L128-L149, whose WHEN OTHER stays last: FC-BAD-DATE-VALUE is matched at L133 and moves 'Datevalue error' at L134, a literal that already fills WS-RESULT PIC X(15) exactly, so no padding is added and one space separates it from TstDate:. Severity and message number are DECODED from that arm's own 88-level VALUE X'000309CC59C3C5C5' (L64) rather than interpolated from a neighbour - the first halfword X'0003' is the severity, the second X'09CC' is 2508, and FACILITY-ID X'C3C5C5' is 'CEE' in EBCDIC - because the nine feedback numbers are non-contiguous (2507, 2508, 2509, 2513, 2517, 2518, 2520, 2521, skipping 2510-2512, 2514-2516 and 2519) and no one of them can be derived from another. The date reaches this arm because June has 30 days, so day 31 overflows the month. This is the other side of the month-length lookup from case07, and the pairing is the reason two cases share message 2508: case07's 2023-02-29 is decided by the Gregorian leap rule, 2023 not being divisible by four making February 28 days long, whereas 31 June is calendar-invariant and needs no leap reasoning at all, because no year in any era has a thirty-first of June. The two together drive both branches of that lookup - the February branch, whose length is computed, and the fixed short-month branch, whose length is tabulated - which one case alone could not, and an implementation that hard-coded 31 days for every month would fail this case while still passing case07. Neither outcome depends on when the suite runs: the month length is taken from the literal month 06 in the input, never from a runtime calendar. Each component is separately legitimate, which is what isolates 2508 from its neighbours: the text is fully numeric where the mask wants digits, so this is not FC-NON-NUMERIC-DATA 2520 (case18, case19); 06 is a real month, so it is not FC-INVALID-MONTH 2517 (case12 to case14); every field the mask asks for is supplied, so it is not FC-INSUFFICIENT-DATA 2507 (case05, case06); and 2022 is far inside the supported range, so it is not FC-UNSUPP-RANGE 2513 (case10, case11). Only the combination is impossible. The echoed date is deliberately WRONG and must stay so: the group move at L122 overwrites the clean copy planted at L107-L108 with WS-DATE-TO-TEST, whose leading two bytes are Vstring-length PIC S9(4) BINARY (L26) holding LENGTH OF LS-DATE, the declared width of a PIC X(10) item and therefore always 10 = X'000A' (L105-L106), so WS-DATE PIC X(10) keeps only those two binary bytes plus the first eight characters, 2022-06-. The '31' that makes the date invalid is discarded, and the message names the error without ever showing the offending value - preserved as legacy behaviour, not repaired. The two non-printables are written here as the explicit escapes for 0x00 and 0x0A so the pair reads as the halfword 0x000A and not as a newline in the data. WS-DATE-FMT (L55) is filled at L111-L113 before the CALL and is not a target of L122, so it stays clean and echoes the mask verbatim. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of the 01 WS-MESSAGE declaration at L42-L57, whose thirteen spans sum to exactly 80, the token at L64, the arm at L133-L134 and the group move at L122; they are never captured from a COBOL run, which is impossible here, one blocker being that no Language Environment CEE* service exists, so the CEEDAYS at L116 cannot be executed and the validator behind it is hand-written.
